Hoster links show their name, size and state as soon as they arrive, Click'n'Load from filecrypt works through the browser extension, and columns move live while you drag them.

## ✨ Added

- **Hoster links show their name, size and state as soon as they arrive.** A rapidgator link or any other hoster link that a debrid service downloads used to sit in the link collector as its bare address, with no size, until it started. KnightLoader now asks the hoster plugins of its headless JDownloader about each new batch at once, the way JDownloader's own link collector does, and fills in the file name, the size and whether the file is online. It costs no traffic and needs no account. Recheck asks them too.
- **The desktop app keeps its Java up to date.** Once a week it asks Adoptium for a newer Temurin 21 for the JDownloader it runs. With Update automatically on the JDownloader row it fetches the new runtime, checks its checksum and moves JDownloader onto it while none of its downloads runs. The old runtime stays until JDownloader has started on the new one, and comes back if it does not. With only Check automatically on, the row tells you that a newer Java is ready.

## 🎨 Design

- **Columns move live while you drag them.** Grab a column head on Downloads or in the link collector and the whole column, head and cells, follows the pointer while the others slide aside. Let go and it settles into its gap, and Escape puts everything back. Alt and an arrow key slide the columns the same way. The order is saved once, when you drop the column, and with reduced motion the columns swap without the slide. On a touch screen, hold a head briefly and then move.
- **KnightLoader follows GlimStone 3.8.5,** which the Components card names. Buttons take the accent under the pointer the way the design language describes it, and the symbols for each kind of file come from its list. Under rainbow the buttons of a page count through the palette in the order they stand, so two buttons side by side on a card no longer light up alike. Glyph buttons and link badges count too, and a button with its own colour keeps it.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The Components card shows what KnightLoader updates or follows:** KnightLoader, yt-dlp, JDownloader and GlimStone. ffmpeg, UnRAR, Java and the built-in libraries ship inside KnightLoader and only show up when one of them is missing. The Java download still shows on the JDownloader row.
- **yt-dlp falls back by itself.** A fetched copy that is gone or does not start makes KnightLoader use the other yt-dlp, and the row says so. The Back to the system copy button is gone.
- **A missing ffmpeg or UnRAR says so where it matters.** A video download that needs ffmpeg and finds none fails as "No ffmpeg", with what to do on the desktop app, in the container and on a self-built install, and it is not retried until ffmpeg is there. A RAR set that fails without UnRAR says so and suggests installing it or setting `KL_UNRAR`.
- **The pinned parts are checked every week.** A weekly check looks for a newer Temurin 21 and UnRAR and proposes the new versions with their checksums. It also notices a new GlimStone release.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Click'n'Load from filecrypt reaches KnightLoader through the browser extension.** filecrypt hands its links over from a small helper window of its own, and two things stopped them there. Inside a container session the helper carries a strict Content-Security-Policy that blocks its own check for JDownloader, so it never sent anything; the page can no longer clear the extension's JDownloader flag. And the window has no toolbar, so the extension could not show its popup there; the popup now opens in the browser window that shows the site, in Firefox and in Chrome alike.
- **Click'n'Load names the program that holds its port.** With JDownloader running, switching Click'n'Load on showed the raw Windows error. KnightLoader now asks the system which program listens on the port and names it, with a short hint on what to close. A KnightLoader that answers for itself can still be taken over.
- **A pasted video page downloads its video.** With "Follow pages and collect the files they link to" on, a pasted page that plays a video and links a few screenshots got crawled for the screenshots, and the video never reached yt-dlp. KnightLoader now asks yt-dlp about the page first. If yt-dlp finds a video or a playlist there, the page goes to yt-dlp and is not crawled. If it finds nothing, the page is crawled for its files as before.
- **A Usenet release that par2 rebuilt counts as done right away.** A file that failed to download and was rebuilt by the repair could still read as failed for a moment after its release passed the check, which an arr app reading the history right then would count as a failed download.

## 🔒 Security

- **The Android app's build tooling takes glob 14.0.2 and minimatch 11.0.1.** They close two advisories: a cancelled glob search could keep walking the file system, and some minimatch patterns could tie it up for a long time.
